mn141:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living at Benares in the Deer Park at Isipatana.
mn141:1.3: There he addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn141:2.1: “At Benares, bhikkhus, in the Deer Park at Isipatana the Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened, set rolling the matchless Wheel of the Dhamma, which cannot be stopped by any recluse or brahmin or god or Māra or Brahmā or anyone in the world—that is,
mn141:2.2: the announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of the Four Noble Truths.
mn141:3.1: “the announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of the noble truth of suffering. the announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of the noble truth of the origin of suffering…of the noble truth of the cessation of suffering…of the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.
mn141:4.1: “At Benares, bhikkhus, in the Deer Park at Isipatana the Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened, set rolling the matchless Wheel of the Dhamma, which cannot be stopped by any recluse or brahmin or god or Māra or Brahmā or anyone in the world—that is,
mn141:4.2: the announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of these Four Noble Truths.
mn141:5.1: “Cultivate the friendship of Sāriputta and Moggallāna, bhikkhus;
mn141:5.3: They are wise and helpful to their companions in the holy life.
mn141:5.6: Sāriputta trains others for the fruit of stream-entry, Moggallāna for the supreme goal.
mn141:5.7: Sāriputta, bhikkhus, is able to announce, teach, describe, establish, reveal, expound, and exhibit the Four Noble Truths.”
mn141:6.2: Having said this, the Sublime One rose from his seat and went into his dwelling.
mn141:7.1: Then, soon after the Blessed One had gone, the venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus thus:
mn141:7.3: “Friend,” the bhikkhus replied to the venerable Sāriputta.
mn141:8.1: “At Benares, friends, in the Deer Park at Isipatana the Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened, set rolling the matchless Wheel of the Dhamma…
mn141:8.2: and exhibiting of the Four Noble Truths.
mn141:9.1: “The announcing…and exhibiting of the noble truth of suffering…of the noble truth of the origin of suffering…of the noble truth of the cessation of suffering…of the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.
mn141:10.1: “And what, friends, is the noble truth of suffering?
mn141:10.2: Birth is suffering; ageing is suffering; death is suffering; sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are suffering; not to obtain what one wants is suffering; in short, the five aggregates affected by clinging are suffering.
mn141:11.2: The birth of beings into the various orders of beings, their coming to birth, precipitation [in a womb], generation, the manifestation of the aggregates, obtaining the bases for contact—
mn141:12.2: The ageing of beings in the various orders of beings, their old age, brokenness of teeth, greyness of hair, wrinkling of skin, decline of life, weakness of faculties—
mn141:13.2: The passing of beings out of the various orders of beings, their passing away, dissolution, disappearance, dying, completion of time, dissolution of aggregates, laying down of the body—
mn141:14.2: The sorrow, sorrowing, sorrowfulness, inner sorrow, inner sorriness, of one who has encountered some misfortune or is affected by some painful state—
mn141:15.2: The wail and lament, wailing and lamenting, bewailing and lamentation, of one who has encountered some misfortune or is affected by some painful state—
mn141:16.2: Bodily pain, bodily discomfort, painful, uncomfortable feeling born of bodily contact—
mn141:17.2: Mental pain, mental discomfort, painful, uncomfortable feeling born of mental contact—
mn141:18.2: The trouble and despair, the tribulation and desperation, of one who has encountered some misfortune or is affected by some painful state—
mn141:19.1: “And what, friends, is ‘not to obtain what one wants is suffering’?
mn141:19.2: To beings subject to birth there comes the wish:
mn141:19.3: ‘Oh, that we were not subject to birth! That birth would not come to us!’
mn141:19.4: But this is not to be obtained by wishing,
mn141:19.5: and not to obtain what one wants is suffering.
mn141:19.9: subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair, there comes the wish:
mn141:19.10: ‘Oh, that we were not subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair! That sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair would not come to us!’
mn141:19.11: But this is not to be obtained by wishing,
mn141:19.12: and not to obtain what one wants is suffering.
mn141:20.1: “And what, friends, are the five aggregates affected by clinging that, in short, are suffering?
mn141:20.2: They are: the material form aggregate affected by clinging, the feeling aggregate affected by clinging, the perception aggregate affected by clinging, the formations aggregate affected by clinging, and the consciousness aggregate affected by clinging.
mn141:20.3: These are the five aggregates affected by clinging that, in short, are suffering.
mn141:20.4: This is called the noble truth of suffering.
mn141:21.1: “And what, friends, is the noble truth of the origin of suffering?
mn141:21.2: It is craving, which brings renewal of being, is accompanied by delight and lust, and delights in this and that; that is,
mn141:21.3: craving for sensual pleasures, craving for being, and craving for non-being.
mn141:21.4: This is called the noble truth of the origin of suffering.
mn141:22.1: “And what, friends, is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering?
mn141:22.2: It is the remainderless fading away and ceasing, the giving up, relinquishing, letting go, and rejecting of that same craving.
mn141:22.3: This is called the noble truth of the cessation of suffering.
mn141:23.1: “And what, friends, is the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering?
mn141:23.2: It is just this Noble Eightfold Path; that is,
mn141:23.3: right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, and right concentration.
mn141:24.2: Knowledge of suffering, knowledge of the origin of suffering, knowledge of the cessation of suffering, and knowledge of the way leading to the cessation of suffering—
mn141:25.2: Intention of renunciation, intention of non-ill will, and intention of non-cruelty—
mn141:26.2: Abstaining from false speech, abstaining from malicious speech, abstaining from harsh speech, and abstaining from idle chatter—
mn141:27.2: Abstaining from killing living beings, abstaining from taking what is not given, and abstaining from misconduct in sensual pleasures—
mn141:28.2: Here a noble disciple, having abandoned wrong livelihood, earns his living by right livelihood—
mn141:29.2: Here a bhikkhu awakens zeal for the non-arising of unarisen evil unwholesome states, and he makes effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives.
mn141:29.3: He awakens zeal for the abandoning of arisen evil unwholesome states, and he makes effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives.
mn141:29.4: He awakens zeal for the arising of unarisen wholesome states, and he makes effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives.
mn141:29.5: He awakens zeal for the continuance, non-disappearance, strengthening, increase, and fulfilment by development of arisen wholesome states, and he makes effort, arouses energy, exerts his mind, and strives.
mn141:30.2: Here a bhikkhu abides contemplating the body as a body, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.
mn141:30.3: He abides contemplating feelings as feelings, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.
mn141:30.4: He abides contemplating mind as mind, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.
mn141:30.5: He abides contemplating mind-objects as mind-objects, ardent, fully aware, and mindful, having put away covetousness and grief for the world.
mn141:31.2: Here, quite secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states, a bhikkhu enters upon and abides in the first jhāna, which is accompanied by applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of seclusion.
mn141:31.3: With the stilling of applied and sustained thought, he enters upon and abides in the second jhāna, which has self-confidence and singleness of mind without applied and sustained thought, with rapture and pleasure born of concentration.
mn141:31.4: With the fading away as well of rapture, he abides in equanimity, and mindful and fully aware, still feeling pleasure with the body, he enters upon and abides in the third jhāna, on account of which noble ones announce: ‘He has a pleasant abiding who has equanimity and is mindful.’
mn141:31.5: With the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and grief, he enters upon and abides in the fourth jhāna, which has neither-pain-nor-pleasure and purity of mindfulness due to equanimity.
mn141:31.7: “This is called the noble truth of the way leading to the cessation of suffering.
mn141:32.1: “At Benares, friends, in the Deer Park at Isipatana the Tathāgata, accomplished and fully enlightened, set rolling the matchless Wheel of the Dhamma, which cannot be stopped by any recluse or brahmin or god or Māra or Brahmā or anyone in the world—that is,
mn141:32.2: the announcing, teaching, describing, establishing, revealing, expounding, and exhibiting of these Four Noble Truths.”
mn141:32.3: That is what the venerable Sāriputta said.
mn141:32.4: The bhikkhus were satisfied and delighted in the venerable Sāriputta’s words.
